description: NERC, the North American Electric Reliability Corporation, runs mandatory data collection systems on the performance of the bulk power system and publishes metrics, indicators and one open database from them. Its Reliability Assessment and Performance Analysis programme covers these systems. Coverage: North America. GADS, started by the industry in 1982 from collection begun in 1963, holds operating and outage information on conventional generating units of 20 MW or more, wind plants of 75 MW or more commissioned since 2005 and solar plants of 20 MW or more, reported quarterly by registered entities. TADS, collected since 2008, records outages of bulk AC circuits, transmission transformers, back-to-back converters and DC circuits, used for metrics on outage frequency, duration and causes. MIDAS collects protection system misoperations, DADS demand response availability, and the Electricity Supply and Demand (ES&D) database is published as a yearly workbook whose contents were not read. Format and access: reporting through OATI and NERC portals limited to registered entities with digital certificates; public outputs are reliability indicator pages, reports and the 2025 ES&D workbook (XLSX, August 2026); unit-level data are requested under Section 1600 of NERC's rules, and document titles on the GADS page refer to limited disclosure and confidentiality requests. Licence: not stated; raw submissions are treated as confidential (terms not read). Caveats: only aggregates and the ES&D workbook are openly downloadable, and the disclosure rules were not read. Simulation uses: failure and outage rates for generators and transmission elements feed reliability, cascading failure, resilience and capacity planning models. Related records: the NERC geomagnetic disturbance data (data-nerc-gmd-gic-magnetometer-event-data) come from the same programme.
